question.problem: We wish to construct a cylindrical can with a base and a lid. Our cylinder must have an exact volume of $686\pi \,{\text{mm}}^{3}.$ What is the smallest surface we can get?
question.worked_solution:
First, let's draw a picture of a cylinder. Let $r$ be the radius, and $h$ the height.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14195873/assets/cec96bdd2335ff5635d11c4ea6016257b35bd5450778a70ecc1f5e0156ccfe9e.png)

We wish to minimize the surface area

$$
S=2\pi rh+2\pi {r}^{2}.
$$

We know that the volume is fixed at $686\pi \,{\text{mm}}^{3},$ so we also have the constraint condition

$$
686\pi =\pi {r}^{2}h.
$$

Now, by making $h$ the subject of the constraint equation, we have that

$$
h=\frac{686}{{r}^{2}}.
$$

Plugging the above into our expression for $S,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}S(r) & =2\pi r(\frac{686}{{r}^{2}})+2\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1\,372\pi }{r}+2\pi {r}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We want to minimize $S,$ so we need to differentiate $S$ and set the derivative equal to zero. The derivative is 

$$
{S}^{′}(r)=-\frac{1\,372\pi }{{r}^{2}}+4\pi r.
$$

Setting the derivative equal to zero and solving for $r$ gives a stationary point, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}^{′}(r) & =0 \\ -\frac{1\,372\pi }{{r}^{2}}+4\pi r & =0 \\ 4\pi r & =\frac{1\,372\pi }{{r}^{2}} \\ 4\pi {r}^{3} & =1\,372\pi  \\ {r}^{3} & =343 \\ r & =\sqrt[3]{343} \\  & =7\,\text{mm}\end{aligned}
$$

Using a calculator, we can verify that if $r<7$ then ${S}^{′}(r)<0,$ and if $r>7$ then ${S}^{′}(r)>0,$ which means that the stationary point $r=7$ is indeed a minimum of $S(r).$

Therefore, the cylinder with the smallest surface area has radius $r=7\,\text{mm}.$

Finally, to find the smallest surface area, we substitute $r=7\,\text{mm}$ into the equation for the surface area $S:$

$$
\begin{aligned}S(7) & =\frac{1\,372\pi }{7}+2\pi (7)^{2} \\  & =294\pi \,{\text{mm}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that the smallest possible surface area of the cylinder is $S=294\pi \,{\text{mm}}^{2}.$
